Suggest a chunk_size for read_vcf() given available RAM

Source: R/VCFArrow-lifecycle.R
vcf_suggest_chunk_size.Rd

Suggest a chunk_size for read_vcf() given available RAM

Usage

vcf_suggest_chunk_size(
  available_gb,
  n_samples,
  fmt_chars = 25,
  sample_chars = 10,
  workers = .vcf_workers(),
  n_columns = NULL
)

Arguments

available_gb

RAM available in gigabytes.

n_samples

Number of samples.

fmt_chars

Average length in characters of a sample's FORMAT text in the VCF (e.g. 24 for "0/1:12,8:20:99:200,0,300"), default 25. Longer FORMAT fields (e.g. PL with many alleles) need more memory.

sample_chars

Average length of the sample names, default 10.

workers

Number of worker processes read_vcf() will use (see vcf_set_workers()), default the number currently set.

n_columns

Deprecated and ignored: the size of a genotype row is now computed from its columns.

Value

Invisibly, the suggested chunk size (integer).

Details

Half of available_gb is left for the operating system, R and later operations; the other half is shared by the chunks read_vcf() holds at once (one per worker). A chunk holds one row per variant and sample, of about 44 + sample_chars + fmt_chars bytes in memory: .row_id, a1 and a2 (4 bytes each), the sample name and the sample's FORMAT text (each 4 bytes plus its characters), phased (1 bit), and DP, GQ and ADR (8 bytes each). The FORMAT text is kept so write_vcf() can write the sample fields unchanged; it is often the largest column. With workers, each chunk's raw VCF lines (about fmt_chars + 1 bytes per genotype) are also held, by the main process and by the worker parsing them. The result is limited to between 1,000 and 500,000 variants.

Examples

vcf_suggest_chunk_size(available_gb = 8, n_samples = 100)
#> ℹ For 8 GB RAM, 100 samples and 1 worker, recommended chunk_size = 500,000
#> (use: read_vcf(vcf_file, chunk_size = 500000))
